To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the grain‐boundary character distributions of undoped and impure magnesium oxide ceramics were investigated by the electron channeling contrast technique.
the grain-boundary plane distribution of MgO can be modified by the presence of certain impurities.
the grain‐boundary character distribution of undoped Mg‐O can be altered by the addition of Ca, Sr and Y, but not Ba, and the effect is most pronounced with Ca.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and implementation of a new approach to the study of the structure and properties of grain boundaries in polycrystalline materials, which is based on the use of a new technique, high‐energy ion channeling, for the determination of grain‐boundary character distributions (GBCDs).
the development of a novel method of controlling the microstructure of materials through the use of impurity additions.
the effects of impurities on the microstructure of MgO.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GBCD is not determined by a single factor, but rather by a combination of factors, which include the impurities, the impurity concentration, and the processing history of the sample.
the segregation of impurity atoms at grain boundaries is an important factor influencing the distribution of GB planes.
the segregation of Ca, Sr and Ba impurities is anisotropic and that the GBCD of MgO can be controlled through the use of impurity additions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
impurities in MgO segregate to the GBs and that the GB plane distributions can change as a result of the segregation.
Ca, Y, and Ba impurities segregate to MgO grain boundaries and that this impurity segregation affects the grain‐boundary plane distribution.
the segregation of impurities at GBs can have an effect on the distribution of GB planes, but that the effect is not universal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
impurities segregating to GBs can change the distribution of GB planes.
the segregation of Ca, Ba and Y to GBs is not a simple function of the ionic size.
the segregation of impurity atoms to GBs in polycrystals can alter the distribution of grain boundary planes, which can have important implications for the mechanical properties of the material.
